core_obligations: Prove (1) by choosing homogeneous generators and picking one of minimal degree d_r; the condition that the positive-degree part times M equals M forces that generator to be zero, and the conclusion follows by induction on the number of generators (proof lines 13481-13484).
Derive (2) by applying (1) to the quotient M/N (proof line 13485), and (3) by applying (2) to the submodule which is the image of N in M together with M itself (proof lines 13485-13486).
Derive (4) by applying (3) to the map from the direct sum of shifted copies of the ring sending basis elements to the given x_i (proof lines 13487-13488).
proof_roadmap: Settle the first assertion by a minimal-degree generator argument (proof lines 13480-13484).
Chain the remaining three assertions to the previous ones (proof lines 13485-13489).
difficulty_reason: The lemma collects four graded forms of Nakayama's lemma: vanishing from S_+M = M for a finite graded module, the submodule version with N + S_+N', surjectivity detected modulo S_+M, and generation by elements generating the quotient by S_+M (statement lines 13466-13478). The proof does not repeat an argument four times: it settles the first assertion by choosing a homogeneous generator of minimal degree, which must vanish because of S_+M = M, and then derives the other three by applying the earlier parts to a quotient, to a pair of submodules, and to a shifted direct sum (proof lines 13480-13489). Deciding which earlier part each later assertion follows from is the content, and the author records each reduction in one clause. H2.
